title: voice-dock-inventory-and-action-beacons
content:
TL;DR: compact inventory of recurring customer asks from the last 6 weeks + pragmatic action beacons we can test in a 2-week spike. This is not exhaustive — lean, prioritized, engineering-friendly.

Context and scope:
- Source windows: support tickets (May 1–Jun 15), weekly CS sync notes, 3 customer calls (FinServeCorp, Searchly, DocuPilot).
- Focus: runtime/serving pain points that block adoption of higher-throughput modes (dedicated/private) and observable asks (latency/cost clarity).
- Goal: produce 3 quick experiments and a draft backlog (~6 items) that eng/product can estimate.

Top recurring asks (short form):
1) "Clear per-route cost estimates" — customers want an easy way to project token spend per endpoint + perf tradeoffs. Example quote: \"We need a per-route cost slider so finance can model our app before committing.\"
   - Why it matters: procurement + self-serve conversion.
   - Quick beacon: add a per-route sample calculator in Console using recent 7-day usage + model profile. UI prototype + lightweight API.

2) "KV cache visibility and invalidation controls" — customers hit stale completions or unexpected memory growth.
   - Impact: correctness risk for multi-session agents.
   - Quick beacon: expose KV cache size per model/route and add a manual invalidation button + TTL hint field. (Spike: API + Console view).

3) "Graceful fallback telemetry" — when we fall back to smaller model variants, customers want an audit trail and signal to their app.
   - Impact: trust, postmortems.
   - Quick beacon: add a header in responses and a per-request note in traces showing which model/variant served; surface in Console trace view.

4) "Deterministic latency windows for cold-starts" — customers see high jitter on first requests after scale-to-zero.
   - Impact: UX for interactive features.
   - Quick beacon: publish a cold-start SLO and a diagnostic endpoint that returns recent cold-start percentiles for a route.

5) "Batching tuning recommendations per workload" — teams uncertain whether to enable larger batches or prefer lower latency.
   - Impact: cost vs latency decisions.
   - Quick beacon: implement a workload profiler (sampling) for 48h that suggests batch sizes and target queueing thresholds; present as a single recommendation card.

6) "More granular alerts for quality regressions" — customers want alerts tied to eval sets/prompts that matter to them.
   - Impact: reduces MTTR on model rollouts.
   - Quick beacon: allow uploading a 50–200 prompt testset to Console, auto-run on canary and send a condensed pass/fail digest.

Opportunity mapping (why these over others):
- Low-effort/high-value: per-route cost estimates (data already available), KV cache surface (runtime metrics exist), fallback telemetry (trace/log plumbing exists).
- Medium effort: workload profiler + canary evals (needs sampling infra).
- Higher effort: cold-start SLO diagnostics (requires aggregating infra signals across autoscaler and runtime).

Engineering notes / implementation hints:
- Per-route cost calculator: backend assemble from per-token unit costs (model profile table) + average tokens per request (7d rolling). UI: one-line card with toggle to see worst-case 95p cost. Link to billing SKU. Ticket: JIRA-PI-789.
- KV cache UI: reuse existing runtime metrics emitted to observability; add a label by route+model. Expose API: GET /routes/{id}/kv-stats. Keep a manual flush: POST /routes/{id}/kv-flush. Minimal auth checks.
- Fallback telemetry: add metadata field in current request tracing span: model.variant.reason=fallback. Emit to traces + response header X-Redwood-Model-Variant. Backfill not required.

Proposed 2-week spike plan (owner suggestions):
Week 1:
- Prototype Console card for per-route cost (frontend + mock API) — owner: Maya
- Runtime: add KV stats endpoint + small aggregation job — owner: Arman
- Trace header POC: add header in runtime response for variant tag — owner: SRE oncall (Liam)
Week 2:
- Wire Console to KV stats endpoint, add manual flush button, basic unit tests
- Surface trace info in Console traces (top-line note + link to span)
- Customer validation: demo to FinServeCorp and Searchly, collect 3-minute feedback loop

Acceptance criteria for spike:
- Console shows per-route estimated cost card using real 7-day data (not mocked).
- KV stats endpoint returns size and hit/miss rates for a chosen test route; manual flush works from Console.
- Response header appears for fallback cases in test harness and is visible in one traced request.

Risks and mitigations:
- Privacy/PII: route-level usage might expose sensitive info — mitigation: only show aggregated cost and require route-level admin perms.
- Runtime load: KV stats aggregation could be heavy — mitigate with sampling and per-minute rollups.
- False confidence in cost estimator: clearly label assumptions and include a conservative multiplier.

Follow-ups and open questions (for product/eng sync):
- Should per-route cost appear in invoices or just on Console? (finance ask)
- TTL/invalidations: do we need per-session scoped caches vs global route cache? (prod design)
- Canary eval size: how large should the prompt set be before we trigger an alert? (SRE + ML)
- Who owns the security review for adding X-Redwood-Model-Variant header? (Security team)

Notes-to-self and ask list for CS reps:
- Demo checklist for initial customers: show cost card, KV stats, and fallback header in a live trace (3–5 mins).
- Collect 3 specific example prompts from each customer that broke due to stale KV or fallback so we can create focused eval sets.
- Tagging: add label "voice-dock:beaconed" to confirmed customer threads in Zendesk.

Raw customer vignettes (anonymized):
- FinServeCorp: \"We turned on batching and saw 35% cost savings but our support agents got wrong context on session 2 — probably cache mismatch. We need visibility.\"
- Searchly: \"When a pod scales from zero our search box returns slow, we don't know if it's us or Redwood. If we could see a cold-start rate we'd know how to work around it.\"
- DocuPilot: \"We had a model fallback during peak and our audit logs didn't show it; compliance flagged it. We need an immutable record.\"

Immediate next steps (this week):
- Get eng alignment on spike owners + tag JIRA tickets (Maya to schedule 30m with Eng-Serving-Runtime).
- Prep demo sketch and test route with sample data (Arman).
- Run internal security quick-check for response header (Liam -> security).

Appendix: quick sketch links and refs:
- Confluence: CONFLUENCE-1234 (voice-dock backlog sketch)
- Slack threads: #cs-runtime-echoes (ongoing customer snippets)
- Example ticket IDs: ZD-5541 (FinServeCorp batching), ZD-5612 (Searchly cold-start)

End notes: this doc is intentionally terse. If we converge on the spike scope I'll expand into a longer spec with API contracts and Console mockups.
